abstract: Audits dive system failure modes and verifies emergency decompression protocols
system_message:
You are the Hyperbaric technical safety authority (HTS), responsible for auditing dive system failure modes and verifying emergency decompression protocols across candidate saturation diving intervention teams.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Australia·Audits dive system failure modes and verifies emergency decompression protocols（SIM）
information_points.content:
HTS-SIM-JAI：Assessed under the auditing regulatory jurisdiction of Australia, North Sea Hyperbaric Operations Consortium received a failure mode effects analysis audit score of 75 points for its mobilized spread, and its contingency decompression protocols validated status is confirmed as true for 135 meters sea water dive profiles.
HTS-SIM-4NY：In the auditing regulatory jurisdiction of Australia, Caledonian Deepwater Diving Alliance recorded a failure mode effects analysis audit score of 85 points regarding system redundancy readiness, with its contingency decompression protocols validated status confirmed as true.
HTS-SIM-TNE：Under the Australia auditing regulatory jurisdiction, Grampian Subsea Specialist Group obtained a failure mode effects analysis audit score of 80 points on spread equipment redundancy, and its contingency decompression protocols validated status is true under local hyperbaric requirements.

information_points.title: United Kingdom·Audits dive system failure modes and verifies emergency decompression protocols（SAFE）
information_points.content:
HTS-SAFE-LY5：Evaluated under the United Kingdom auditing regulatory jurisdiction, Grampian Subsea Specialist Group attained a failure mode effects analysis audit score of 80 points on spread redundancy, and its contingency decompression protocols validated status is recorded as true for the 135 meters sea water profile.
HTS-SAFE-H8U：Within the United Kingdom auditing regulatory jurisdiction, Caledonian Deepwater Diving Alliance registered a failure mode effects analysis audit score of 85 points on mobilized saturation spread redundancy assessments, while its contingency decompression protocols validated status is confirmed as true for 135 meters sea water profiles.
HTS-SAFE-DB3：Under the auditing regulatory jurisdiction of the United Kingdom, North Sea Hyperbaric Operations Consortium achieved a failure mode effects analysis audit score of 90 points based on offshore safety standards across bell handling and gas mixing panels, and its contingency decompression protocols validated status is true for target profiles at 135 meters sea water.
